subject: reasoning
question: Mr. I starts from Point M and drives 5 km towards the south. He then takes a right turn, drives 8 km, turns left and drives 7 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 12 km. He takes a final left turn, drives 12 km and stops at Point N. How far (shortest distance) and towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point M again? (All turns are 90 degree turns only unless specified.)
solution:
Given, 

Mr. I starts from Point M and drives 5 km towards the south.

He then takes a right turn, drives 8 km, turns left and drives 7 km.

He then takes a left turn and drives 12 km.

He takes a final left turn, drives 12 km and stops at Point N.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a59a5255b1c16ea1a5dbe1856bce647f86197e15040d0c47f70a8b1acf730e21.png] 

So, Point N is 4 km East of Point M.

To reach Point M from Point N, Mr. I needs to drive 4 km towards the West.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".
